_about: The v1b bridge as built, pin by pin, read off the bench's eye (tools/eye.py views at zoom 500, docs/eye-views.json).
done: the wire at this pin was seen in the right hole. check: built, but it reads wrong or the eye cannot settle it; the note says what to look at.
A pin not listed is not built yet, and the marked sheet leaves it in full colour.
Drawn by tools/wiring-diagram.py into docs/wiring-v1b-build.svg; a key that names no pin on the sheet stops the tool.
BASELINE 2026-09-13 15:40 EDT: the camera fixed in place, the wiring as the user left it. Later reads are compared against this one.

FIFTH LOOK 2026-09-14 12:06 EDT: the J1 to U3 chain wired (the /PL link and the eight Q lines). A wire's end stands a few millimetres proud of the board and the eye looks at it from one side, so a raised end reads up to half a pitch from its hole; a landing is settled where the bare end is seen at the hole, and left as a check where it is not.

SIXTH LOOK 2026-09-14 13:55 EDT: the user moved the second wire off U3-5 and pushed the brown home; both re-read with the map's holes projected onto fresh close looks. The boards had moved again on the desk (126 px down), so the map was shifted, not re-read.

RIG BASELINE 2026-09-15 01:10 EDT: the BRIO on the metal frame, straight down, the whole board in one frame (captures/b8-all.jpg); the hole map read afresh; the named views re-aimed (they stand turned 90 degrees against the earlier sets). Read against the rig set (captures/views-20260915T010318, captures/grid8): every pin done before reads the same; the UNO batch is read below.

LOOKED AGAIN 2026-09-15 01:26 EDT after the user reported the SPI leads re-routed and D5 seated in column 34: the board frame and the U3 and U1 close-ups differ from the baseline set only by sensor noise (worst 40 px block mean difference 18 of 255, against 182 when the camera turned), so the change had not reached the board when these were taken. The checks stand until the morning's look.

SECOND RIG POSE 2026-09-15 01:45 EDT: the UNO's leads re-run direct from its header and the boards shifted right. The map was read off the new frame by tools/board-overlay.py --read (every hole found, the rows and columns fitted, the views re-aimed) and every landing read on tools/view-rings.py projections. LIMIT met here: a Dupont housing hides which of its positions is loaded, and a raised object reads outward from the frame's centre (about one pixel per 5 mm of height per 100 px of offset), so a housing that stands across two columns cannot be settled from above; those pins stay checks for the meter or the side eye.

METERED 2026-09-15 EDT by the user: U1-1 and the three SPI pins on U3 checked for continuity with a meter after the second rig pose. The eye reads the housings as before (it cannot settle a housing's positions); the meter can, and did.

A check on a pin the map does not place (the UNO's, the console lead's) may carry "at": {"col": N, "side": "rail"|"middle"|"rails"} naming the place on the board its note is about; the overlay circles that spot.
MIDDLE BOARD MAPPED 2026-09-15: the map covers the middle board (docs/board-map.json, `parts`: J2 and R1 placed where the eye reads them); their pins are listed here from this look on.

THIRD RIG POSE 2026-09-15 13:16 EDT: the boards rearranged on the frame (the chip board at the top, its rails along the frame's top edge, the middle board below it, a fourth rail-only board at the bottom); the map re-read by --read with new bands. R2 and C4 (the clock pin's filter, added by the user this afternoon) went on the schematic and are looked for here.
PLACEMENTS 2026-09-15: state "plan" is a placement asked for and not built (green on the photograph, listed with the checks on the sheet); the note is the instruction.

rails.note: Rails read right with the lead ends in the holes: orange + and brown GND from the left board to the middle board; one red link from the left board's GND column to the right board's GND column (a red wire on GND), one from the middle board's + to the right board's +. The UNO's 5 V and its ground (through USB) power all three boards' rails; the console's port +5 V (J1-5) is not carried, so the two supplies meet only at ground, as designed.

observations: RIG, SECOND POSE: the boards shifted right on the frame; the map re-read automatically (tools/board-overlay.py --read) and every view re-aimed; the rings sit on the holes out to column 50.

The middle board is mapped (its rows read the other way up: a to e toward the right board, f to j toward its own rails, the pair below). The five-way housing at columns 9 to 13 is the power and reset breakout's, parked, joined to nothing (the user, 2026-09-15); a 2-by-4 black header stands at the board's left end (columns 58 to 60, rows f to h) and a 4-way header on its rail rows near columns 50 to 53, both with pin tips up.
The Q pairing is PROVEN 2026-09-15 23:00: the walk of every single bit through the 595 came back on D0 at its own position, so each grey line joins the 595 output to the 165 input the sheet says.

The UNO now sits at the frame's top right on a blue screw-terminal shield, its leads running direct: a bundle (purple, blue, cream, red) down over the top rail to U3's rails side and on, a red to the +5V rail at column 5, and white, yellow and orange to the pad's housing on the middle board. The screw shield hides the header's pin labels, so which UNO pin each lead leaves is not readable on camera.

The two-pin black header across the rail rows at column 27 is a probe point for metering the rail voltage (the user, 2026-09-15): its two pins are not joined to each other, and it is not the UNO's feed.
Orientation settled: the notch and the pin-1 dot of U1, U2 and U3 all face the high-column end, as the map places them.
Two yellow ceramic capacitors stand across the rails at columns 28 and 17; the plan puts one 100 nF beside each chip. The value is not readable on camera.
A red link from the top GND rail row at column 12 runs down to the board's other rail pair: correct but red.
